title: Everyday Math
description: Math you actually use: percentages, discounts & tax, units, plus ratios and scale.

stations.title: Percentages
stations.summary: Percent means 'per hundred' — the most used tool when shopping and reading the news.
points: Shortcuts: 10% = divide by 10; 1% = divide by 100; 25% = a quarter; 50% = a half.
'Up 20%' means multiply by 1.2. 'Down 20%' means multiply by 0.8.
A percentage always refers to something: 5% of a salary ≠ 5% of a car price.

questions.prompt: A price of 250,000 gets a 20% discount. You pay...
A price rises from 80,000 to 100,000. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explain: The increase is 20,000 on a starting value of 80,000 → 20,000/80,000 = 0.25 = 25%. Always divide by the original value.

stations.title: Discounts & Tax
stations.summary: Final price = price after discount, then plus tax. The order matters.
points: Stacked discounts are not added: 50% then 20% is not 70%.
Value added tax is added to the pre-tax price, not the discounted-then-taxed total twice.
Excluding tax → multiply by (1 + rate). Including tax → divide by (1 + rate).
Always compare unit prices (per gram/litre), not the package price.

questions.prompt: A 200,000 shirt is discounted 25%. What is the price after discount?
An item costs 300,000 before tax and VAT is 11%. Total paid?
Stacked discounts: 400,000 gets 50% off, then a further 20% off the new price. Final price?

cards.back: Apply one after another, never add them up

stations.title: Units & Conversion
stations.summary: Unit mistakes cost real money — from recipes to building projects.
points: Metric ladder: km → hm → dam → m → dm → cm → mm (each step down ×10).
1 kg = 1,000 g; 1 litre = 1,000 ml; 1 hour = 3,600 seconds.
Speed conversion: km/h → m/s divide by 3.6 (and multiply by 3.6 to go back).
Area uses squared units (m²), volume uses cubic units (m³ or litres).

questions.prompt: A car travels at 36 km/h. How much is that in m/s?
questions.explain: 36 ÷ 3.6 = 10 m/s. Remember: km/h to m/s means divide by 3.6.

questions.prompt: A recipe needs 0.75 kg of flour. How many grams?

cards.back: Divide by 3.6 · m/s → km/h multiply by 3.6

stations.title: Ratios & Scale
stations.summary: Ratios help you sort things out: what is cheaper, faster, or closer.
points: A ratio reads in order: 3 : 2 means the first part is 3 and the second is 2.
A map scale of 1 : 100,000 means 1 cm on the map = 100,000 cm = 1 km on the ground.
Speed = distance ÷ time. Time = distance ÷ speed.
To compare prices, make the units the same first (for example, price per 100 g).

questions.prompt: On a 1 : 200,000 map, a distance of 4 cm equals how many kilometres on the ground?

questions.explain: 500 g at 20,000 equals 40,000/kg, which is more expensive than 38,000/kg.

questions.prompt: A 120 km trip takes 2 hours. What is the average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 km ÷ 2 h = 60 km/h.

cards.back: 1 cm on the map = 1 km on the ground
